params:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US

- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Weather requests current location for forecasts but does not link the location to your Apple ID. The forecast service uses rotating tokens to ensure your location queries are not traceable to you.

Key points:
- Location used only for the current forecast
- No persistent location history retained
- Queries not linked to Apple ID

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Gmail Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Google LLC's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Gmail processes email content for spam filtering, security threat detection, and feature suggestions like Smart Compose. Google has stated it does not use email content for advertising, though metadata around your account is part of the broader Google ad-targeting profile.

Key points:
- Email content processed for spam and security
- Smart Compose / Smart Reply use ML on your messages
- Google does not target ads based on email content
- Google account profile incorporates Gmail usage signals

Apple Music Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Apple Music collects only listening behaviour, library content, and identifiers needed for the service. No third-party tracking, no ad targeting. Standard Apple privacy posture.

Key points:
- No data used for cross-app tracking
- No third-party advertising
- Listening history kept on-device where possible
- Standard Apple ID deletion controls

- Searches not linked to Apple ID
- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising

TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

Apple Maps Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Apple Maps processes location and search queries with random rotating identifiers — your searches are not tied to your Apple ID and are stripped of identifiers within 24 hours. One of the more privacy-preserving mapping options.

Key points:
- Searches not linked to Apple ID
- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

Notes stores content on-device by default, with end-to-end encrypted iCloud sync as opt-in. No advertising data, no analytics on note content, no third-party processors.

- No content analysis or advertising
- Sync requires explicit iCloud opt-in

Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

Gmail Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Google LLC's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Gmail processes email content for spam filtering, security threat detection, and feature suggestions like Smart Compose. Google has stated it does not use email content for advertising, though metadata around your account is part of the broader Google ad-targeting profile.

Key points:
- Email content processed for spam and security
- Smart Compose / Smart Reply use ML on your messages
- Google does not target ads based on email content
- Google account profile incorporates Gmail usage signals

Apple Maps Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Apple Maps processes location and search queries with random rotating identifiers — your searches are not tied to your Apple ID and are stripped of identifiers within 24 hours. One of the more privacy-preserving mapping options.

Key points:
- Searches not linked to Apple ID
- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

Gmail Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Google LLC's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Gmail processes email content for spam filtering, security threat detection, and feature suggestions like Smart Compose. Google has stated it does not use email content for advertising, though metadata around your account is part of the broader Google ad-targeting profile.

Key points:
- Email content processed for spam and security
- Smart Compose / Smart Reply use ML on your messages
- Google does not target ads based on email content
- Google account profile incorporates Gmail usage signals

- Standard Apple ID deletion controls

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Apple Maps Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Apple Maps processes location and search queries with random rotating identifiers — your searches are not tied to your Apple ID and are stripped of identifiers within 24 hours. One of the more privacy-preserving mapping options.

Key points:
- Searches not linked to Apple ID
- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

Notes Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Notes stores content on-device by default, with end-to-end encrypted iCloud sync as opt-in. No advertising data, no analytics on note content, no third-party processors.

Key points:
- Note content stored on-device or end-to-end encrypted
- No content analysis or advertising
- Sync requires explicit iCloud opt-in

- Event content not analysed for advertising
- Email-based suggestions processed locally

Weather requests current location for forecasts but does not link the location to your Apple ID. The forecast service uses rotating tokens to ensure your location queries are not traceable to you.

Key points:
- Location used only for the current forecast
- No persistent location history retained
- Queries not linked to Apple ID

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
TikTok Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for TikTok Ltd.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

TikTok’s privacy practices are wide-ranging: it collects identifiers, location, viewing patterns, and content interactions, and uses much of this for cross-app tracking and ad targeting. The policy describes complex data flows including overseas transfers that some regulators have flagged.

Key points:
- Builds detailed engagement profiles from viewing behaviour
- Tracks across third-party apps and websites
- Transfers data internationally including outside the EU/US
- Limited control over algorithmic content personalisation

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Spotify Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Spotify AB's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Spotify collects listening behaviour, identifiers, and contact info to personalise recommendations and serve advertising on the free tier. Premium users see less ad-related processing. The policy is clear about what’s collected and why.

Key points:
- Listening data drives personalised recommendations
- Free-tier users have ad data shared with partners
- Clear opt-outs available for marketing communications
- Standard 30-day deletion window after account closure

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
WhatsApp Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption for message content, but collects metadata — who you talk to, how often, from where. Phone number and contacts are linked to your identity and shared with Meta’s broader infrastructure for ad personalisation outside the message stream itself.

Key points:
- Message content end-to-end encrypted
- Metadata (contacts, frequency, location) shared with Meta
- Phone numbers linked across Meta’s ad platforms
- Limited data retention policies for metadata

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Gmail Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Google LLC's real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Gmail processes email content for spam filtering, security threat detection, and feature suggestions like Smart Compose. Google has stated it does not use email content for advertising, though metadata around your account is part of the broader Google ad-targeting profile.

Key points:
- Email content processed for spam and security
- Smart Compose / Smart Reply use ML on your messages
- Google does not target ads based on email content
- Google account profile incorporates Gmail usage signals

Apple Music collects only listening behaviour, library content, and identifiers needed for the service. No third-party tracking, no ad targeting. Standard Apple privacy posture.

- No third-party advertising
- Listening history kept on-device where possible
- Standard Apple ID deletion controls

privacy_policy_analyses.source_text:
Apple Maps Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Apple Maps processes location and search queries with random rotating identifiers — your searches are not tied to your Apple ID and are stripped of identifiers within 24 hours. One of the more privacy-preserving mapping options.

Key points:
- Searches not linked to Apple ID
- Identifiers rotated to avoid long-term profiling
- Location data processed locally where possible
- Personalised features available without identification

Notes Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Apple, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Notes stores content on-device by default, with end-to-end encrypted iCloud sync as opt-in. No advertising data, no analytics on note content, no third-party processors.

Key points:
- Note content stored on-device or end-to-end encrypted
- No content analysis or advertising
- Sync requires explicit iCloud opt-in

- Event content not analysed for advertising
- Email-based suggestions processed locally

- No persistent location history retained
- Queries not linked to Apple ID

params:
Instagram Privacy Policy (sample)

This sample document stands in for Meta Platforms, Inc.'s real privacy policy so the demo can exercise the summary pipeline without fetching anything.

Instagram collects an extensive range of personal data — identifiers, location, browsing and search history — and uses much of it to track users across other companies’ apps and websites. The privacy policy permits sharing with Meta’s ad partners and acknowledges that some data may be retained after account deletion.

Key points:
- Tracks users across third-party apps for advertising
- Collects precise location and contact information
- Shares data with Meta’s broader advertising network
- Account deletion does not immediately remove all data
